body_text: PDF Version STEINHAUSEN, Switzerland, Feb. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Transocean Ltd. (NYSE: RIG) today reported financial results for the fourth quarter and full year of 2025. The Company will hold a conference call and webcast at 9 a.m. EST, 3 p.m. CET, on Friday, February 20, 2026, to discuss the results, with participation details included in this release. In addition, supplemental slides have been posted to the Investors section of the Company’s website at www.deepwater.com . 2025 KEY POINTS Operating revenues were $3.965 billion, up 13% from $3.524 billion in 2024. Revenue efficiency(1) was 96.5%, up from 94.5%. Net loss attributable to controlling interest was $2.915 billion, $3.04 per diluted share. Adjusted EBITDA of $1.37 billion, up from $1.148 billion or 19%. Cash flows from operations were $749 million, up $302 million or 68%. Free cash flow was $626 million, up $433 million from $193 million. Total principal amount of debt reduced to $5.686 billion, down $1.258 billion or 18%. Total liquidity of $1.507 billion, including undrawn revolving credit facility. Added $839 million in contract backlog(2) at a weighted average dayrate of $453,000. “During 2025, we took significant strides to strengthen our capital structure, sustainably lowering costs, and ensuring we continue to deliver best in class service to our customers around the world,” said President and Chief Executive Officer, Keelan Adamson. “At just shy of 98%, we delivered our best uptime performance on record while making significant progress in strengthening our balance sheet by retiring approximately $1.3 billion in debt principal and saving nearly $90 million in annualized interest expense. “In 2026, Transocean achieves its 100th year as a company. As we proudly celebrate this centennial milestone, our primary objective will be to exceed our customers’ expectations by delivering safe, efficient, and reliable operations, thereby creating value for our shareholders. “We believe that our recently announced definitive agreement to combine with Valaris is entirely consistent with these objectives. Customers and investors alike will benefit from the expanded fleet of best-in-class, high-specification rigs and strong pro forma cash flow which improves our financial flexibility, enables accelerated debt reduction, and continued investment in our people, assets, and technologies to enhance the delivery of our services.” FULL YEAR 2025 FINANCIAL SUMMARY Years ended December 31, sequential 2025 2024 change (In millions, except per share amounts and percentages) Contract drilling revenues $ 3,965 $ 3,524 $ 441 Revenue efficiency 96.5 % 94.5 % Operating and maintenance expense $ 2,406 $ 2,199 $ (207 ) Net loss attributable to controlling interest $ (2,915 ) $ (512 ) $ (2,403 ) Basic loss per share $ (3.04 ) $ (0.60 ) $ (2.44 ) Diluted loss per share $ (3.04 ) $ (0.76 ) $ (2.28 ) Adjusted EBITDA $ 1,370 $ 1,148 $ 222 Adjusted EBITDA margin 34.6 % 32.5 % Adjusted net income (loss) $ 37 $ (54 ) $ 91 Adjusted diluted earnings (loss) per share $ 0.04 $ (0.26 ) $ 0.30 Net loss attributable to controlling interest was $2.915 billion, $3.04 per diluted share. Cash provided by operating activities was $349 million, up 42% compared to prior quarter and was primarily related to working capital improvements. Contract drilling revenues were $1.043 billion, up 1.5% compared to prior quarter, primarily related to improved rig utilization, partially offset by slightly lower revenue efficiency across the fleet. Operating and maintenance expense was $605 million, up 3.6% compared to prior quarter, primarily related to four rigs undergoing recertifications or shipyard maintenance, partially offset by lower costs on rigs sold or classified as held for sale. Interest expense was $132 million, excluding the effect of the bifurcated exchange feature of the 4.625% exchangeable bonds due 2029, down 6% compared to prior quarter, primarily due to our debt reduction efforts achieved in the fourth quarter. Capital expenditures were $28 million. The Effective Tax Rate(3) was 68.8%, up from (1.4)% in the prior quarter. The increase was primarily due to losses on rig impairments in the prior quarter. Excluding discrete items, the Effective Tax Rate was 72.3% compared to 34.8% in the previous quarter. Cash taxes paid in the period were $18 million. We believe that such non-GAAP measures, when read in conjunction with our operating results presented under U.S. GAAP, can be used to better assess our performance from period to period and relative to performance of other companies in our industry, without regard to financing methods, historical cost basis or capital structure. Such non-GAAP measures should be considered as a supplement to, and not as a substitute for, financial measures prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP. All non-GAAP measure reconciliations to the most comparative U.S. GAAP measures are displayed in quantitative schedules on the company’s website at: www.deepwater.com . ABOUT TRANSOCEAN Transocean is a leading international provider of offshore contract drilling services for oil and gas wells. The company specializes in technically demanding sectors of the global offshore drilling business with a particular focus on ultra-deepwater and harsh environment drilling services and operates the highest specification floating offshore drilling fleet in the world. Transocean owns or has partial ownership interests in and operates a fleet of 27 mobile offshore drilling units, consisting of 20 ultra-deepwater drillships and seven harsh environment semisubmersibles. For more information about Transocean, please visit: www.deepwater.com . NOTES Revenue efficiency is defined as actual operating revenues, excluding revenues for contract terminations and reimbursements, for the measurement period divided by the maximum revenue calculated for the measurement period, expressed as a percentage. Maximum revenue is defined as the greatest amount of contract drilling revenues the drilling unit could earn for the measurement period, excluding revenues for incentive provisions, reimbursements and contract terminations. The contract backlog represents the maximum contract drilling revenues that can be earned considering the reported operating dayrate in effect during the firm contract period. Effective Tax Rate is defined as income tax expense or benefit divided by income or loss before income taxes. title: Introducing Navan Edge — Built by Travel Experts, Powered by AI
summary: Navan shares an update on Navan Edge, our boundary-pushing, AI-powered executive assistant built for frequent business travelers. Here’s what to know.
body_text: Navan Edge is now available on iOS. Click here to learn more and get started. Navan was founded more than a decade ago because business travel was broken — the road warriors driving business forward didn’t have access to the tools they needed. Fixing that, of course, is the whole reason Navan exists, and we’ve come a long way. Today, more than 3,000 Navan employees are continuously innovating to make travel easy for business travelers at the 10,000-plus companies we serve. We’re more than ten years in, and in many ways we’re just getting started, finding new ways to improve the experience for every frequent traveler. Today, I’m excited to share that we’re opening early access to our newest product: Navan Edge. Navan Edge is the executive assistant that every business traveler wants, but very few have. Imagine every road warrior receiving proactive, thoughtful support that learns how you like to travel, helps you book the perfect trip, and fixes issues before they become problems. We’re building Navan Edge for two groups of travelers. First, travelers who work for companies that have a corporate travel tool, but one that’s so frustrating and limiting, they end up booking around it. That leaves them dealing with the fallout — like unexpectedly canceled hotel reservations after a long flight — on their own. And the second group, which we are focused on for this early access, is frequent business travelers who don’t have a dedicated booking tool. They do the research on travel and the legwork of managing their bookings, loyalty programs, and adjustments all themselves. This second group makes up what we call the unmanaged business travel market. And it’s enormous, accounting for approximately $56 billion of the estimated $86 billion total addressable business travel market . We’re designing Navan Edge to give this group the kind of business travel experience they deserve — one that no one else can offer. At the Center of Navan Edge: Transformative AI Navan has always pushed the boundaries of what AI can do, and Navan Edge puts that effort on full display. To start, Navan Edge will focus on helping frequent business travelers find the perfect hotel, through a UX that mirrors how they use AI in their day-to-day lives. When searching for flights, hotels and restaurants, travelers can just use natural language. What Navan Edge gives back isn’t generic information. It provides personalized recommendations that best match the traveler’s preferences: loyalty programs, favored airplane seats and amenities, proximity to the office, nearby coffee shops, and the details that matter — like whether the hotel gym opens early enough for their 6 a.m. routine or if a room with blackout curtains is available. They can also then book directly within their chat. Now imagine that same level of personalization and proactivity across the entire travel experience. Soon, Navan Edge will come to the rescue for flight disruptions. Knowing when and how travelers like to fly, it will find the best alternatives for their situation and ask them to pick one. It’s that easy. And if the delay means arriving at their hotel hours later than planned, Navan Edge will help ensure the reservation isn’t canceled. At all times, we have human agents standing by who get a full summary of the problem or special request so they can jump on it to finish the job. So What’s Next? We’re looking forward to seeing what some of the world’s most demanding road warriors think of this product in the coming weeks. The Navan Edge roadmap is focused on taking personalization, proactivity, and the level of service across all booking types to the next level, and integrations with new suppliers Our proprietary AI (powered by Navan Cognition ), decades worth of data, and passion for not just meeting but exceeding the needs of frequent travelers have gotten us to this point. And like I said, in many ways we’re just getting started. There’s more to come as we take business travel to the next level by making it more personal, more modern, and easier for every frequent traveler. At Navan, it’s what we do. title: Vendor Payments: Invoice vs Contract? Vendor Payments Decoded
summary: Vendor payments in India made easy: learn invoice vs contract for bank compliance, documents for outward remittance, & invoice proof+agreements speed approval.
body_text: Key takeaways Banks clear outward remittances faster when your invoice proof clearly ties to a permitted purpose code, and your documents confirm party identity, transaction genuineness, and AML compliance. An invoice alone is usually fine for one off, post delivery payments under USD 10,000, SaaS renewals with plan evidence, and repeat vendors with clean history. Pair invoice plus agreement for advances or retainers, milestone or long duration engagements, IP or license related payments, high values above USD 50,000, and when paying individuals. Submit a complete pack every time: KYC, Form A2 with correct purpose code, invoice proof, agreement or statement of work when needed, vendor bank details, and tax forms like 15CA or 15CB if applicable. Tie the invoice description and SAC or HSN codes to the chosen purpose code, mismatches are the most common reason for Requests for Information. Respond precisely to compliance queries, avoid bulk document dumps, and keep a reusable remittance template to reduce cycle time. Platforms like Karbon Business can simplify incoming international receipts and documentation, while your AD bank processes outward remittances with predictable approvals. Why banks ask for documents: the compliance framework behind vendor payments Under FEMA and RBI oversight, authorized dealer banks must verify that every outward remittance is legitimate. Compliance teams validate four pillars before releasing funds: purpose validity, party authenticity, transaction genuineness, and AML or KYC compliance. If you send only a vague invoice with mismatched names or no scope, the transfer gets flagged, and the back and forth begins. Bottom line : The clearer your evidence of what you bought, from whom, and why it fits a permitted purpose, the faster your vendor gets paid. Definitions: invoice proof, agreement, and vendor payments Invoice proof is a formal payment request that identifies seller and buyer, describes what was delivered, lists unit rates and totals, states currency and dates, and shows the seller’s bank details. Proforma invoices are valid for advances, final tax invoices for post delivery payments, PDFs from your accounting tool, or portal receipts all qualify if they are specific. Agreement covers signed contracts, statements of work, purchase orders, acceptance of terms of service, or compiled email threads that confirm scope and terms. For SaaS, clickwrap works when paired with an order confirmation that references the terms URL and plan. Vendor payments are outward remittances for services, goods, licenses, or subscriptions. Classification, service versus goods, recurring versus one time, influences which documents your bank prioritizes. Invoice vs contract for vendor payments: when each document is sufficient When an invoice alone usually suffices One off, post service invoices : The deliverable already exists, the invoice describes it specifically, for example, “Custom website redesign, 3 pages, responsive layout, 10 revisions included.” Low to medium values : Under USD 10,000 with clean data and a matching purpose code typically clears quickly. SaaS renewals or subscriptions : Invoice plus a quick screenshot of the plan or service page often does it, the invoice should show the plan and billing period. Repeat vendors : Prior successful transfers shorten review for similar new invoices. Red flags to avoid : round number totals without itemization, missing vendor address, no invoice date, name mismatches between invoice and beneficiary. When banks ask for an agreement as well Advances or retainers : Pair a proforma invoice with a statement of work or contract that explains milestones and payment schedule. Milestone or long duration engagements : A master services agreement gives compliance the context they need. IP, licensing, or royalty like payments : Provide license terms or vendor terms of service that explain permitted use and fees. High value transfers : Above USD 50,000, a signed agreement reduces ambiguity. Paying individuals : A contract or email agreement reassures the bank the transaction is commercial and genuine. Missing bank details on invoice : Add a bank details confirmation or include them in the agreement to verify the beneficiary. Documents for outward remittance: complete checklist KYC and identity : PAN, address proof for individuals, business PAN and registration for entities. Form A2 and purpose code : Choose the correct code, for example P0801 consulting, P0802 IT services, P0810 professional services, P0820 licenses or subscriptions. Invoice proof : Clear description tied to the purpose code, currency, unit rate, totals, dates, and seller bank details, IBAN, SWIFT, bank address. Agreement or contract : Signed contract, SOW, PO, or compiled email thread, and for clickwrap, add order confirmation referencing the terms URL. Vendor bank details verification : Beneficiary name, account number, IBAN, SWIFT or BIC, bank address, consistent with the invoice. Tax forms if applicable : 15CA or 15CB based on your CA’s guidance and bank thresholds. For goods : Bill of Entry, shipping bill, import license if relevant. For subscriptions : Invoice plus plan or pricing page screenshot, and terms link if requested. Any compliance declarations : FEMA declaration, TCS proof, or “not for prohibited use” confirmations, when asked. Pro tip : Package everything as one PDF where practical, invoice first, agreement second, bank details third. This minimizes follow ups. How to create a bank ready invoice proof Exact legal names and addresses for seller and buyer, matching bank records and Form A2. Tax IDs : Seller GSTIN if any, buyer PAN or GSTIN. SAC or HSN codes that align with your purpose code, for example SAC 998312 software development, SAC 998313 professional and technical activities. Currency, unit rate, total , with itemization that looks commercially reasonable. Invoice date and payment terms that explain whether this is advance, immediate, or post delivery. Seller bank details : IBAN, SWIFT, beneficiary name, bank address, exactly as provided by the vendor. Signature or stamp helps authenticity, even if digital. Match description to purpose code to avoid RFIs. Avoid : vague lines like “services rendered,” no itemization, round totals without context, missing address, or loan like terms. What qualifies as a strong agreement Parties and effective date , with jurisdictions named. Scope of work or deliverables with specifics that prove reality. Milestones and schedule tied to payment tranches. Fees and payment terms in clear currency and timing. Termination and liability to show a balanced, commercial contract. Signatures and dates , digital signatures are widely accepted. Clickwrap evidence for SaaS, include subscription screenshot, features, terms URL, and order confirmation. Email threads compiled in a single chronological PDF, with final acceptance visible. Step by step: sending an outward remittance that clears first time Identify the purpose code , for example P0802 for design or coding, P0801 for consulting, P0820 for licenses or subscriptions. Prepare the document pack , invoice plus agreement if advance, recurring, high value, or an individual beneficiary. Confirm tax position , check 15CA or 15CB needs with your CA, bank thresholds vary. Submit to your AD bank , complete Form A2, attach invoice, agreement, and beneficiary details, and share a contact for quick RFI resolution. Track and respond fast , answer only what compliance asks, precision beats volume. Remember : When in doubt, include the agreement, it rarely slows a file and usually accelerates approval. Timelines and costs for outward remittance Processing time : typically two to five working days after approval, one to two days for some faster corridors, add time for compliance queries. Fee heads : TT charges, correspondent bank fees, forex markup depending on your bank, ask for the all in cost. TCS : common rate is 5 percent above ₹7 lakhs per financial year for LRS non business categories, business to business cases can differ, confirm with your CA. Common rejection reasons and quick fixes Mismatched names : Align buyer name across invoice, Form A2, and bank records. Advance without agreement : Add a statement of work or contract with milestones. Purpose code mismatch : Make invoice wording and SAC align with the chosen code. Incomplete bank details : Get IBAN, SWIFT, beneficiary name, bank address on vendor letterhead. Missing 15CB on high values : Consult your CA and provide forms per bank policy. Unverifiable vendor : Request registration certificate, tax ID, or ID proof for individuals. Proforma without SOW : Pair it with a detailed scope and timeline. Scenarios: Indian freelancers and founders in action Scenario 1: paying a US UI or UX designer a milestone payment Decision : An advance needs an agreement. Prepare : proforma invoice for the advance, plus a short SOW with deliverables and dates. Submit : Form A2 with P0802, attach bank details. Outcome : approval in two to three days, later post delivery invoice clears even faster. Scenario 2: SaaS subscription renewal stuck in compliance review Issue : Invoice alone lacked context. Fix : add your subscription page screenshot, order confirmation, and terms of service link. Resubmit with P0820 or P0802 as applicable. Outcome : cleared within one day. Scenario 3: advance to a video editor overseas for a long term project Decision : Individual beneficiary, advance, recurring, agreement is essential. Prepare : MSA or email SOW PDF with schedule and acceptance. Submit : proforma invoice, agreement, Form A2, beneficiary details. Outcome : three to four days, predictable approvals thereafter. Tools for managing international vendor payments Karbon Business : multi currency accounts in USD, GBP, EUR, CAD, automatic e FIRA in twenty four hours, flat 1 percent platform fee, zero FX markup using mid market rates, hold currency up to sixty days to manage risk. Use it for inward receipts, then settle outward payments via your AD bank for full control. Wise Business : transparent multi currency accounts, pay vendors locally in their currency. Payoneer : send and receive cross border funds across multiple currencies. RazorpayX International : Indian business focused tools for international payouts and documentation. Tazapay : B2B cross border with escrow and compliance automation for larger contracts. Evaluate fees, supported corridors, documentation workflows, and settlement speed against your volume and vendor mix. Final checklist: build your remittance template The core rule : if payment precedes delivery, involves an individual, is recurring or high value, add the agreement. A tidy pack, invoice, agreement, bank details, correct purpose code, plus any tax forms, wins first time approvals. Create a reusable SOW template with milestones and payment triggers. Maintain a master checklist for KYC, Form A2 , invoice, agreement, vendor bank details, and tax forms. Store verified beneficiary details securely, update when vendors change banks. Respond to RFIs same day, keep replies specific and complete. Understand invoice versus contract requirements, prepare a complete submission, and convert compliance from a bottleneck into a predictable workflow. Your vendors get paid on time, your cash flow remains smooth, and your team avoids last minute scrambles. FAQ Invoice bhejna enough hai kya for outward remittance, ya bank will ask for contract also? If the work is already delivered, the invoice is specific, and the amount is modest, many banks clear with invoice only. If it is an advance, long duration, high value, or you are paying an individual, attach an agreement or SOW to avoid delays. Form A2 fill karte waqt P0802 aur P0820 me kaunsa choose karun for design plus software tools? Use P0802 for services like design, coding, or IT work, and P0820 for licenses and subscriptions. If your payment includes both, split invoices or ask your bank which code they prefer based on the dominant component. Freelancer ko advance dena hai, proforma invoice kaafi hai kya without contract? For advances, a proforma invoice should be paired with a short statement of work or contract showing deliverables, milestones, and payment schedule. Without that, banks often raise an RFI and hold the funds. Digital signature chalega kya, DocuSign or Adobe Sign wale agreements accept hote hain? Yes, Indian banks generally accept properly executed digital signatures. Submit the PDF signed by both parties, and ensure names match the invoice and beneficiary details to keep compliance simple. SaaS subscription ke liye har month bank poochta hai proof, kya bheju taaki baar baar stop na ho? Along with the invoice or receipt, add a screenshot of your account page showing plan name and price, plus the terms of service link. This combo usually clears renewals smoothly, especially when the vendor and amounts are consistent month to month. High amount, like USD 60,000 services payment ke liye kya extra documents lagenge? Yes, high values trigger deeper review. Share the signed agreement or MSA, detailed invoice with itemization, correct purpose code, and check with your CA about 15CA or 15CB. This context reassures compliance and avoids multiple RFIs. Individual contractor ko pay kar raha hu abroad, bank AML risk batata hai, isse kaise clear karun? Provide a clear SOW or contract, identity proof if the bank asks, and a detailed invoice with scope and hours. Specifics reduce AML concerns by proving it is a legitimate commercial engagement. 15CA or 15CB ki need kab hoti hai for services remittance, and kya Karbon Business help karta hai? Requirements vary by bank and amount, many banks ask for 15CB beyond certain thresholds for services. Your CA should advise based on nature of service and treaties. Karbon Business can streamline incoming client payments and documentation, while you use your AD bank for outward remittances along with the required tax forms. Purpose code aur invoice description mismatch ho gaya, ab kya karu, payment stuck hai? Either update the invoice description to match the chosen purpose code, or request your bank to change the code to the accurate one. Add SAC or HSN codes to strengthen the alignment and resubmit promptly. Vendor invoice me bank details incomplete hain, kya alternate proof chalega? Ask the vendor for a bank details confirmation on letterhead, or a signed document that lists beneficiary name, account number, IBAN, SWIFT, and bank address. Consistency with the invoice name is critical for approval. Repeated SaaS renewals ke liye har baar documents bhejna padta hai, koi smarter way? Create a single PDF pack with the latest invoice, a persistent plan screenshot, and the terms link. Save it as your template and submit with each renewal, most banks clear quickly once they recognize the file pattern. International clients se payment aata hai Karbon Business par, vendors ko pay bank se karta hu, kya yeh acceptable process hai? Yes, many Indian freelancers and founders receive funds via Karbon Business for speed and documentation, for example e FIRA, then use their AD bank for outward remittances. Keep your inward and outward documents aligned, purpose codes correct, and approvals stay predictable.

title: Electric mobility: TotalEnergies and Tikehau Capital Join Forces to Develop Public Charging Networks in Belgium and the Netherlands

This partnership will support municipal authorities through the EV transition and consolidate TotalEnergies’ position as a leading player […]
body_text: Paris, February 4, 2026 – TotalEnergies and Tikehau Capital have announced the creation of a joint investment platform to promote the development of charging infrastructure for electric vehicles in urban public spaces in Belgium and the Netherlands. This partnership will support municipal authorities through the EV transition and consolidate TotalEnergies' position as a leading player in public charging in Benelux. The platform is equally owned by TotalEnergies and Tikehau Capital and aims to: pursue the development of public concessions that are currently under construction or in operation by TotalEnergies in several major Belgian and Dutch cities; respond to new calls for tender that expand the urban public charging infrastructure in Belgium and the Netherlands. TotalEnergies will bring its expertise to develop, operate and maintain public charging infrastructure powered exclusively by certified renewable energy. TotalEnergies will also leverage its partnership with Tikehau Capital to strengthen its business model in electric mobility, benefiting from Tikehau Capital's capital contribution and the sharing of investments, costs and risks. TotalEnergies is a major player in public charging with over: 9,500 operated charge points in Belgium , where the Company is the market leader; 18,000 operated charge points in the Netherlands , putting it among the country's leading players. “We are delighted to sign this new partnership with Tikehau Capital, allowing us to accelerate the deployment of public charging infrastructure in Belgium and the Netherlands and to expand our footprint in these pioneering EV markets,” said Mathieu Soulas, Senior Vice President, New Mobilities at TotalEnergies . “Partnering with TotalEnergies to develop the public charging networks in Belgium and the Netherlands fully reflects our policy of investing in infrastructure that drives the energy transition forward. The joint platform will facilitate access to efficient, sustainable charging solutions, helping take carbon out of the transport sector,” said Emmanuel Laillier, Chief Investment Officer of Private Equity at Tikehau Capital .

Tangible book value per share increased $5.03, or 31.8%, from $15.80 at December 31, 2024 to $20.83 at December 31, 2025 (see “Non-GAAP Financial Measure Reconciliation” below for additional detail). These increases were due to earnings growth during the twelve months ended December 31, 2025 and a reduction of unrealized losses in the available for sale securities (“AFS”) portfolio coupled with net proceeds of approximately $43 million from completion of a follow-on common stock offering during the second quarter of 2025. “I am pleased to announce momentum we saw through the first three quarters of 2025 continued through year end,” said Orange County Bancorp President and CEO Michael Gilfeather, “resulting in record earnings of $12.4 million, or $0.93 per basic and diluted share, and $41.6 million, or $3.33 per basic and diluted share, for the fourth quarter and full year, respectively. These figures represent a $5.3 million, or 73.5%, increase in net income over the same quarter last year and $2.4 million, or 24.1%, increase over $10.0 million of net income last quarter. I am equally pleased they represent material contributions from every division of the Bank. Total loans grew $14.6 million during the fourth quarter, and a solid $134.5 million, or 7.4%, for the full year as we continued to prudently manage credit in today’s interest rate environment. This increased our loan portfolio from $1.8 billion at the end of 2024 to $2.0 billion at year end 2025, a figure we aspired to just a handful of years ago. As always, I thank our committed employees and our customers and shareholders for their continued confidence and support.” Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2025 Financial Review Net Income Net income for the fourth quarter of 2025 was $12.4 million, an increase of $5.3 million, or 73.5%, from net income of $7.2 million for the fourth quarter of 2024. The increase represents a combination of increased net interest income and noninterest income as well as a reduction in noninterest expense offset by an increased provision for credit losses over the same quarter last year. Net income for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025 was $41.6 million, as compared to $27.9 million for the same period in 2024. The increase reflects the continued effect of net interest income growth combined with increased non-interest income as well as a reduced provision for credit losses during 2025 as compared to the prior year. The improvement in the provision for credit losses during 2025 as compared to 2024 was the result of lower specific reserves associated with nonperforming loans. The increase in non-interest income includes the recognition of a gain associated with the sale of a branch location coupled with a Bank Owned Life Insurance gain related to policy proceeds from a death benefit. Net Interest Income For the three months ended December 31, 2025, net interest income rose $5.3 million, or 22.8%, to $28.3 million, versus $23.1 million during the same period last year. The increase was driven primarily by a $3.3 million increase in interest and fees on loans during the current period. For the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, net interest income reached $104.1 million, representing an increase of $12.3 million, or 13.4%, over the twelve months ended December 31, 2024. Total interest income rose $3.1 million, or 9.7%, to $35.3 million for the three months ended December 31, 2025, compared to $32.2 million for the three months ended December 31, 2024. The increase reflected a 12.0% growth in interest and fees associated with loans and a 2.1% increase in interest on Federal Funds Sold and other assets. For the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, total interest income rose $7.8 million, or 6.1%, to $135.0 million as compared to $127.2 million for the twelve months ended December 31, 2024. Total interest expense decreased $2.2 million during the fourth quarter of 2025, to $7.0 million, as compared to $9.1 million during the fourth quarter of 2024. The decrease was primarily due to the continued reduction of interest costs associated with lower FHLB advances and borrowings as well as brokered deposits due to increased customer deposit levels during the quarter. Interest expense associated with FHLB advances drawn and other borrowings during the current quarter totaled $264 thousand as compared to $1.9 million during the fourth quarter of 2024. Interest expense related to time deposits totaled $958 thousand during the fourth quarter of 2025 as compared to $1.7 million during fourth quarter 2024. During the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, total interest expense fell $4.5 million, to $30.9 million, as compared to $35.5 million for the same period last year. Provision for Credit Losses The Company recognized a provision for credit losses of $1.6 million for the three months ended December 31, 2025, as compared to a net recovery of $51 thousand for the three months ended December 31, 2024. The current quarter provision included a charge-off of certain commercial and industrial loans and specific reserves associated with certain non-accrual loans as well as loan growth during the quarter. The 2024 recovery was due primarily to slower loan growth during the 2024 fourth quarter combined with the effect of lower reserves associated with certain types of loans closed during fourth quarter 2024. The allowance for credit losses to total loans was 1.45% as of December 31, 2025 versus 1.44% as of December 31, 2024. For the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, the provision for credit losses for loans totaled $7.8 million as compared to $9.6 million for the twelve months ended December 31, 2024. The twelve months ended December 31, 2024 did include a credit provision associated with the recovery of $1.9 million related to Signature Bank subordinated debt which was previously written off. No reserves for investment securities were recorded during the twelve months of 2025 or 2024. Noninterest Income Noninterest income rose $383 thousand, or 8.9%, to $4.7 million for the three months ended December 31, 2025 as compared to $4.3 million for the three months ended December 31, 2024. The growth included increased fee income in each of the Company’s fee income categories, including investment advisory income, trust income, and service charges on deposit accounts. For the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, noninterest income increased $7.2 million, to $23.2 million, as compared to $16.0 million for the twelve months ended December 31, 2024. The twelve month period in 2025 also included BOLI proceeds of $3.6 million and $932 thousand of insurance proceeds related to a claim for a previous fraudulent incident as well as a $1.2 million gain related to the sale of a branch location, partially offset by a $568 thousand loss connected to a $15 million repositioning of our investment securities portfolio. The decrease in noninterest expense for the current three-month period was mainly due to expenses in fourth quarter 2024 related to a fraudulent incident at one of our branches as well as costs associated with litigation related to a nonperforming loan participation. For the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, our efficiency ratio also improved to 53.4% from 60.5% for the same period in 2024. The Company continues to invest in growth, primarily within salaries and benefits, occupancy costs, information technology, deposit insurance, and other operating expenses. Financial Condition Total consolidated assets increased $149.5 million, or approximately 6.0%, during 2025 to $2.7 billion at December 31, 2025. Growth of the balance sheet included increases in cash, loans, and deposits offset by paydowns of borrowings during the current twelve-month period. Total cash and due from banks increased from $150.3 million at December 31, 2024, to $204.2 million at December 31, 2025, an increase of approximately $53.9 million, or 35.9%. This increase resulted primarily from increases in deposit balances and managed loan growth which elevated cash levels while reducing short-term borrowings. Total investment securities decreased $28.2 million, or 6.2%, from $453.5 million at December 31, 2024 to $425.3 million at December 31, 2025. The decrease continues to be driven primarily by investment maturities and paydowns during the twelve months of 2025. Total loans increased $134.5 million, or 7.4%, from $1.8 billion at December 31, 2024 to $2.0 billion at December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by an increase of $118.0 million related to commercial real estate loans, $18.3 million increase in commercial real estate construction loans, and a $7.2 million increase in commercial and industrial loans as well as a $5.3 million increase in home equity loans offset by decreases in the residential real estate and consumer loan categories during 2025. Total deposits increased $157.0 million, reaching $2.3 billion at December 31, 2025, from $2.2 billion at December 31, 2024. This increase was due primarily to $74.5 million of growth in non-interest bearing demand accounts, an $88.5 million increase in interest bearing demand accounts, and an $88.4 million increase in savings accounts. The increases in deposit accounts were offset by a $32.4 million decrease in money market accounts as well as a $62.0 million decrease in certificates of deposit, mainly associated with brokered deposits utilized by the Bank for short term funding purposes. title: Pagaya Launches 2026 Capital Markets Activity with $800M Consumer Loan ABS
body_text: Represents Pagaya’s 85th ABS transaction and largest securitization since November 2024 Reinforces Pagaya’s position as a leading issuer in the U.S. personal loan ABS market NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Feb. 4, 2026-- Pagaya Technologies LTD. (NASDAQ: PGY) ("Pagaya" or “the Company”), a global technology company delivering AI-driven product solutions for the financial ecosystem, today announced the closing of a $800 million AAA rated, personal loan ABS transaction (PAID 2026-1). A total of 32 unique investors participated in the personal loan securitization, with the majority returning from prior transactions. PAID 2026-1 garnered significant investor demand, allowing a 33% upsize from its initial $600 million target size, highlighting continued depth of demand in the consumer credit ABS market for Pagaya’s AI-enabled assets. Since 2018, Pagaya has issued more than $34.5 billion across 85 ABS transactions with over 150 institutional investors, supporting originations across personal loan, auto, and POS programs. “This transaction reflects the steady demand we continue to see from institutional investors for well-structured consumer credit ABS,” said Sahil Chandiramani, Head of Capital Markets at Pagaya Technologies LTD. “Our programmatic issuance approach and the scale of our network allow us to access the securitization market in a consistent and disciplined manner across market environments. The investor participation and execution of this AAA-rated transaction support our ongoing ability to fund high-quality consumer credit assets as we move through 2026.” About Pagaya Technologies Pagaya (NASDAQ: PGY) is a global technology company making life-changing financial products and services available to more people nationwide, as it reshapes the financial services ecosystem. By using machine learning, a vast data network and an AI-driven approach, Pagaya provides comprehensive consumer credit and residential real estate products for its partners, their customers, and investors. Its proprietary API and capital solutions integrate into its network of partners to deliver seamless user experiences and greater access to the mainstream economy. Pagaya has offices in New York and Tel Aviv. For more information, visit pagaya.com . (NYSE: HGTY), an automotive enthusiast brand and leading specialty vehicle insurance provider, announced today financial results for the three and twelve months ended December 31, 2025. “2025 was a standout year for Hagerty, defined by accelerating momentum and record new business count. Top-line gains of 17% were fueled by written premium growth of 14%, and we efficiently converted this revenue into a 91% surge in net income. We also reinvested significantly in our business, including our technology transformation, the launch of Enthusiast+, the roll-out of State Farm to 27 states, as well as our Marketplace expansion into Europe,” said McKeel Hagerty, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of Hagerty. “In 2026, we will continue to invest back into our member-centric model to drive durable, compounding growth, with written premiums expected to increase 15% to 16%. 2026 also marks a major milestone for Hagerty as we move to a 100% quota share with our long-term partner, Markel. We believe this evolution, combined with our technology-led efficiency initiatives, positions us to generate even higher rates of underlying profit growth and cash flow for our shareholders over the coming years,” added Mr. Hagerty. title: How to Create an Invoice: Templates and Best Practices for 2026
summary: Learn how to create invoices that get paid faster. Discover templates for B2B, recurring, and project billing—plus the common errors causing 61% of late payments.
body_text: Invoices are the keystone of accounts receivable. They determine whether your sale becomes cash flow or gets stuck in payment limbo. Every subsequent process (such as payment reminders or collection calls) traces back to decisions made when that invoice was created. Get it right, and payments flow smoothly. Get it wrong, and you're fighting an uphill battle from day one. The stakes are significant. Right now, half of all B2B invoiced sales are overdue across the United States—representing billions in delayed cash flow. While market conditions and customer behavior play a role, much of this payment friction stems from preventable issues that originate at the invoice level. Unlike external factors you can't control, invoice optimization is entirely within your power. Small changes to how you structure, present, and deliver invoices can accelerate payment cycles and reduce the percentage of overdue accounts. This guide focuses on practical, proven techniques that convert revenue to cash faster—because a sale isn't complete until the money hits your account. The Anatomy of an Invoice That Gets Paid A well crafted invoice guides the reader through every piece of information they need to process payment quickly. Yet most invoices fail this basic test, creating friction that transforms a simple transaction into a drawn-out collection process. Every invoice requires the fundamentals like your complete business information, the customer's billing details, a unique invoice number, the invoice date, detailed line items, clear payment terms, and the total amount due. These are bare minimum for a document that accounting departments can actually process. Invoices that get paid on time versus those that languish in approval workflows often differ in two critical elements that businesses routinely overlook: purchase order references and comprehensive payment instructions. When your invoice lands on an accounts payable clerk's desk without a PO number, it immediately gets flagged for additional review. When payment instructions offer only one method (say, checks only), you may be forcing customers into their slowest payment channel. The stakes are higher than most business owners realize. Invoice errors account for 61% of late payments , mostly coming from simple mistakes. These include wrong addresses, missing purchase order numbers, incorrect pricing, and vague service descriptions. If someone in accounting needs to pick up the phone to clarify anything on your invoice, that invoice has failed. Every question they have to ask extends your payment cycle. Every missing piece of information adds days to your cash conversion timeline. Invoice Templates by Use Case Different business models require different invoicing approaches. While the core elements remain consistent, you must present information to match how your clients expect to see their charges broken down. Standard B2B Invoice The standard B2B invoice is your baseline. Every other template builds on this foundation, so getting these elements right matters more than any stylistic choice you'll make. Your Business Information Start with the basics at the top: legal business name, address, phone, email, and your EIN or tax ID. AP departments verify vendor identity before releasing payment. An invoice from an unrecognized sender gets flagged for review or discarded entirely. If you're not already in their vendor system, that missing tax ID blocks setup completely—and of course, no setup means no payment. Customer Information This is where invoices most commonly fail. You need the customer's legal billing name (not the contact's name, DBA, or the parent company unless that's who pays), the correct billing address, and their purchase order number. Enterprise AP departments operate on three-way matching: they compare the PO, the invoice, and the receiving report before releasing payment. Without a PO reference, your invoice won’t match. Then it’ll sit in a queue until someone manually hunts down the paperwork. At many companies, that means it doesn't get paid until someone complains. Invoice Identifiers These establish the payment timeline. Your invoice number should be unique and sequential—duplicates trigger fraud alerts, and non-sequential numbers complicate reconciliation. The invoice date starts the payment clock, but don't assume customers know when that clock ends. Spell out the explicit due date. Saying "Net 30" alone creates ambiguity. Does that mean Net 30 from invoice date? From receipt? From goods delivery? Finally, state the exact date payment is expected. Line Items Specificity matters a lot here. "Consulting services - $5,000" triggers clarification requests. "Strategy workshop, 8 hours @ $625/hr, December 15" gets approved without callbacks. List quantities, unit prices, and line totals separately. Three-way matching compares these against the PO, and discrepancies of even a few cents can trigger manual review. Totals Make the amount due unmissable. AP analysts process dozens of invoices daily. If you bury your total in small text at the bottom of a dense page, it’s way more likely your invoice gets set aside for "later review." Separate subtotal, tax, and final amount. We recommend that you bold the total due or otherwise make it visually prominent. Payment Information List every payment method you accept: ACH, wire, check, credit card. Include complete bank details for electronic payments such as routing number, account number, bank name. Add a payment portal link if you have one; companies using embedded payment links see 3-5 day reductions in time-to-payment. And include a remittance address for checks. Over 40% of B2B payments are still paper, so don't make customers hunt for where to send them. Terms Close with late payment penalties (stated penalties create urgency and legal enforceability), early payment discounts (2/10 Net 30 represents a 36.7% annualized return for customers who take it), and dispute instructions (without a clear process, customers default to non-payment when they have questions). ‍ Standard B2B Invoice Element What to Include Why It Matters Your Business Info Business name & logo Legal business name, logo, branding AP departments verify vendor identity before releasing payment. Invoices from unrecognized senders get flagged for review or discarded. Contact info Address, phone, email When AP has a question, they need to reach you. No contact info means the invoice sits until someone tracks you down—or doesn't. Tax ID / EIN Federal Employer ID Number Companies can't issue payment to vendors not in their system. Missing EIN blocks vendor setup entirely. Customer Info Bill To Customer's legal name + billing address Invoices addressed to the wrong entity or location get returned or routed incorrectly. Large companies have dozens of billing addresses. Ship To Delivery address (if different) AP performs three-way matching: PO, invoice, and receiving report. Ship-to address confirms goods arrived where expected. PO Number Customer's purchase order reference Enterprise AP departments reject invoices without PO references. The invoice has no matching authorization—it sits in a queue until someone manually locates the paperwork, if they bother. Invoice Details Invoice number Unique sequential identifier Duplicate invoice numbers trigger fraud alerts. Non-sequential numbers make reconciliation harder for both parties. Invoice date Date issued Payment terms calculate from this date. A Net 30 invoice dated January 1 is due January 31—but only if the date is clear. Due date Explicit date payment is expected "Net 30" alone creates ambiguity. Net 30 from invoice date? From receipt? From goods delivery? Spell out the exact due date. Payment terms Net 30, 2/10 Net 30, etc. Without stated terms, customers default to their own payment cycle—often 45-60 days regardless of your expectations. Line Items Description Specific product/service details "Consulting services - $5,000" triggers questions. "Strategy workshop, 8 hours @ $625/hr, Dec 15" gets approved without callbacks. Quantity & Unit price How many × price per unit Three-way matching compares invoice quantities and prices against the PO. Discrepancies—even $0.01—can trigger manual review. Line total Qty × Unit Price per line Explicit math lets AP verify calculations instantly. Missing line totals force manual recalculation before approval. Tax Sales tax per line or total Incorrect tax rates create compliance issues. Tax-exempt customers need exemption certificates referenced; taxable customers need accurate rates by jurisdiction. Totals Subtotal Sum of line items before tax Separating subtotal from tax lets AP verify both independently. Bundled totals obscure whether tax was calculated correctly. Tax amount Total tax due Customers need this separated for their own tax reporting. Bundled into the total, it creates extra work on their end. Total Due Final amount—bold, large, prominent AP clerks process dozens of invoices daily. If the total isn't immediately visible, your invoice gets set aside for "later review." Payment Info Payment methods ACH, wire, check, credit card Different companies have different payment capabilities. Offering only wire transfer when a customer's policy requires ACH means delays while they request exceptions. Bank details Routing #, Account #, Bank name For ACH and wire payments, missing bank details mean the customer literally cannot pay you electronically—even if they want to pay today. Payment portal link URL to pay online A clickable payment link removes every friction point between "approved" and "paid." Companies using embedded payment links see 3-5 day reductions in time-to-payment. Remittance address Where to mail checks Over 40% of B2B payments are still paper checks. No remittance address means the customer has to look it up—or the check goes to the wrong location. Terms & Conditions Late payment penalty e.g., 1.5%/month after due date Stated penalties create urgency and provide legal basis for collection efforts. Unstated penalties are unenforceable in most jurisdictions. Early payment discount e.g., 2% if paid within 10 days 2/10 Net 30 represents a 36.7% annualized return for customers who take it. Cash-rich companies actively seek these discounts. Dispute instructions How to raise issues/questions Without a clear dispute process, customers default to non-payment when they have questions. A stated process channels issues to resolution instead of limbo. ‍ Progress/Milestone Invoice Construction and project-based work operate on different payment rhythms than standard transactions. You're billing for work in progress, not completed deliveries, which means your invoice needs to document where the project stands beyond just what you're charging. Billing Period and Completion Status Every progress invoice must clearly state the billing period covered and the percentage of work complete. "Invoice for November 2024" isn't enough. State the specific work performed during that period and how it maps to the overall project scope. Include cumulative totals showing what's been billed to date versus the total contract value. AP departments reviewing a $50,000 invoice need to see immediately that this represents billing 5 of 12 on a $600,000 contract, with $200,000 previously billed and $350,000 remaining. Retention Most construction contracts withhold 5-10% of each payment until project completion. Your invoice must show this math explicitly: gross amount earned, retention withheld, and net amount due. Don't bury retention in footnotes. A contractor billing $100,000 with 10% retention should show the $100,000 earned, the $10,000 withheld, and the $90,000 due this period—plus cumulative retention held to date. When the retention release comes, that running total determines your final payment. AIA Format For commercial construction, the AIA G702/G703 forms are effectively mandatory. General contractors and owners expect this standardized format, and submitting invoices in any other structure creates friction. The forms document schedule of values, work completed by line item, stored materials, and retention calculations in a format every construction AP department recognizes. If you're a subcontractor, your billing must align with how the GC bills the owner. Misaligned billing cycles or format mismatches delay your payment until the GC reconciles the discrepancy. Change Orders Project scope changes during construction—that's inevitable. Your invoice must clearly separate original contract work from approved change orders, referencing the specific change order numbers and approval dates. Unapproved changes billed as standard work get rejected. Approved changes billed without documentation get flagged for verification. ‍ Progress / Milestone Invoice Element What to Include Why It Matters Project Identification Project name Official project title from contract Large GCs manage dozens of active projects. Without clear project identification, your invoice routes to the wrong PM or sits unassigned. Contract number Original contract or subcontract reference Links this invoice to the governing agreement. AP needs this to verify you're authorized to bill and at what rates. Application number Sequential pay application (e.g., #5 of 12) Tracks where you are in the billing cycle. Missing sequence numbers create confusion about what's been paid vs. what's outstanding. Billing Period & Progress Billing period Start and end dates covered "Invoice for November" isn't enough. Overlapping or unclear periods cause duplicate payment disputes and audit flags. Percent complete Overall project completion percentage Owners and GCs compare your claimed completion against their field observations. Significant discrepancies trigger inspections and payment holds. Work performed this period Description of completed activities Justifies why you're billing what you're billing. Vague descriptions like "continued work" invite scrutiny and clarification requests.
